subject: Availability rider: proposed service-commitment schedule, audit evidence & on-call routing
messages:
From: Eileen Carter <eileen.carter@synergiamed.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: availability rider + evidence scope for enterprise MSA

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Synergia is excited about Redwood's routing and autoscaling features. Procurement asked me to start the conversation about an availability rider we need to attach to the enterprise MSA before we route finance. High level asks from legal/procurement: 

- A firm monthly uptime commitment for production endpoints (we proposed 99.95% global availability).
- Latency SLO for P95 generation within our lane (target: <= 350ms across US regions) with defined measurement windows.
- An exception path for burst events tied to documented regional incidents (we understand the need for carve-outs but need predictable thresholds).
- Evidence cadence: procurement wants to receive a 7-day telemetry snapshot + rolling 12mo availability summary on request; ideally held in escrow or a shared audit folder to support audits.

Can your team propose: a) draft rider language for an appendix, b) what would Redwood provide as telemetry evidence (formats, retention), and c) how on-call routing / notification will work for high-severity incidents?

We have a narrow approval window — would appreciate a draft by Friday (2028-09-15). Attaching our standard procurement checklist.

Attachments: synergia_procurement_checklist.xlsx

Best,
Eileen Carter
Head of Procurement, Synergia Health
E: eileen.carter@synergiamed.com
T: +1 415-555-0192

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: availability rider + evidence scope for enterprise MSA

Hi Eileen — thanks for the clear list. Looping in David (Contracts) and Jordan (Sales Ops) to align on legal language and operational runbooks. We can meet your Friday draft target; below is the proposed scope from my side to confirm before we produce a redline: 

Proposed deliverables:
- Draft availability rider (appendix) with uptime target, latency measurement definitions, and excusal/force-majeure carve-outs.
- Evidence package: weekly telemetry export (JSON), monthly availability rollup (CSV), and an ops incident timeline PDF on request. We can stage a 7-day sample export for you to review.
- On-call/notifications: primary on-call team + secondary regional fallback, SRE paging via PagerDuty. We'll include an escalation matrix and expected response vs. resolution target definitions.

Questions for you (to include in the draft):
1) Is Synergia okay with the evidence export format being NDJSON for time-series telemetry?
2) Will procurement accept a 30-day retention for the directly-exported weekly telemetry we provide, with longer-term summarized retention (12 months) for rollups and SLA history?

David/Jordan — can you confirm legal constraints (minimum wording, credit schedule) and whether Sales Ops needs a different measurement window for latency?

I will produce the initial rider draft and a 7-day telemetry sample by EOD Thursday (2028-09-14) to give Synergia a day to review before Friday. If that timeline works, I’ll put the DocuSign route in parallel.

Regards,

Hannah Schmitt

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Eileen Carter <eileen.carter@synergiamed.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Sep 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: availability rider + evidence scope for enterprise MSA

Hannah — thanks for taking point. A few legal/contract items to flag so the rider draft doesn't get caught in iterative redlines: 

- Metric definitions: we must define "availability" precisely (per-route 5-minute measurement windows, tie to successful 2xx responses excluding known maintenance windows). If Synergia wants a global 99.95% that applies to a defined set of production API endpoints, we need an appendix to enumerate those endpoints (or an anchor to the order form).
- Credits: propose a stepped service credit schedule (e.g., 99.90-99.95 = partial credit; below 99.90 = higher credit). We should avoid open-ended unlimited credits — cap on monthly credits as % of monthly invoice to manage exposure.
- Evidence escrow: we can provide encrypted telemetry exports to a shared drive for audit, but full raw KV cache contents or customer payloads are not producible. We should state format (NDJSON), the retention windows (30 days raw, 12mo summarized), and provide a statement about redaction of customer payloads.
- Incident classification: define sev1/sev2 thresholds and expected "acknowledge" SLAs (e.g., acknowledge within 15 minutes for sev1) and whether an "outage" triggers automatic credits.

I will attach a redline with contract language and a suggested credit table — please review for commercial fit before we send to Synergia.

-David
David Kim
Director, Legal & Contracts
Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwoodinference.com

From: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv.sharma@sysopspro.com>

Subject: Re: Request: availability rider + evidence scope for enterprise MSA

Hi all — Rajiv from Synergia's platform team. Quick responses to Hannah/David's questions and a sample export link below.

1) NDJSON is fine for us — our audit team can consume that. We prefer timestamps in ISO-8601 UTC and a clear routing tag per request (region + model + route).
2) Retention: procurement's ask for 12 months of summarized rollups is non-negotiable; raw 30-day retention is acceptable if you provide a signed export on request for longer-term audits.

Link: https://synergia-secure-share.example.com/telemetry-sample-7d (sample NDJSON, anonymized)

Notes on latency measurement: we measure P95 on request-response times excluding streaming/partial tokens. For fairness, we ask Redwood to include both aggregated P95 and a regional P95 for each provisioning lane.

Also, we'd like the rider to include a short runbook excerpt describing the on-call page flow — e.g., primary SRE -> regional lead -> account escalation. Can Redwood provide a one-page runbook excerpt attached to the rider?
